solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Where publicans may be bottled up?

definitions.text: Where publicans may be bottled up?

parts.words: Where publicans may be bottled up?
parts.note: publicans work behind the counters of pubs, and 'bottled up' hints at being locked away in jail, so the phrase serves both a pub and a prison

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about where landlords stash themselves among the bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in prison is idiomatically described as being locked up behind the cell's metal rails.

clue.text: Shoot nuisance besieging a city

indicators.note: besieging means surrounding, so the shoot-plus-nuisance pair is wrapped around the single letter

parts.note: a shoot on a plant is a bud
a nuisance is a pest

explanation.surface: A pest besieging a city, as if an army of insects were laying siege.
explanation.walkthrough: 'besieging' wraps the shoot-and-nuisance pair around the A, so the A sits at the join between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital city of Hungary, straddling the Danube.

clue.text: Couple of journalists given the chop

parts.note: a hack is a journalist
ED is the usual abbreviation for an editor, another journalist

explanation.surface: Two reporters have been sacked from their newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'couple' is two different journalists: a HACK and an ED (editor).
explanation.definitionFit: Something hacked has been chopped at roughly, as with an axe or blade.

clue.text: Una's as troublesome in the capital

indicators.note: troublesome suggests the letters are unruly and must be put into a new order

parts.note: taken letter for letter, including the S

explanation.surface: A woman named Una is causing trouble in the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's of Una's counts as a letter: UNAS plus AS gives the six letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau is the capital city of the Bahamas, so it fits 'the capital' as an example.

clue.text: Commission makes bankrupt vent anger

parts.note: someone bankrupt is broke
to vent anger is to rage

explanation.surface: A bankrupt person's fury drives them to an act of vandalism or protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Brokerage is the fee or commission charged by a broker for arranging a deal.

clue.text: Seems troubled three times during the course

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of the first word are stirred into a new order

parts.note: TER is Latin for three times, a term used in prescriptions and music

explanation.surface: Things seem bad on three separate occasions while a course is under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'times' looks like multiplication, but 'three times' is the Latin word familiar from prescriptions; 'troubled' shuffles the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A semester is a half-year term of study at a college or university, a course period.

clue.text: Stay for beginning of party

parts.note: to be for something is to be pro it

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, here of the party

explanation.surface: Someone decides to stay at a gathering just as it starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a support or brace, and so is a prop.

clue.text: Sea-creature I propose doctoring!

indicators.note: doctoring means tampering with, so the letters are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone suggests treating a marine animal, like a vet at an aquarium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctoring' rearranges the eight letters of I PROPOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A porpoise is a small toothed marine mammal related to dolphins.

clue.text: Unfolded diagram featuring no internal walls

parts.note: something unfolded is open
a plan is a diagram

explanation.surface: An architect spreads out a floor plan for a space without partitions.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-plan office or home has large shared areas without dividing partitions.

clue.text: Verdict is in code to be unravelled

indicators.note: unravelled means untangled, so the letters must be teased apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A court's ruling is hidden in a cipher that someone must crack.
explanation.definitionFit: A verdict is a judgement or ruling, which is a kind of decision.

clue.text: Two men were clearly noticeable

parts.note: Mark is a man's name
Ed is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A pair of men stood out conspicuously.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'two men' are two separate names, MARK and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: A marked difference is one that is clearly evident or pronounced.

clue.text: Ready with material cut out in advance

parts.note: PRE is the prefix meaning before or in advance
pared means trimmed, with material cut away

explanation.surface: A dressmaker is ready, having cut out the fabric beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: Dressmakers' 'material' misleads: the cut-away material is what paring removes, and the clue gives the pieces in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: To be prepared is to be ready for something.

clue.text: Gently at an angle outside, it is very wet

indicators.note: outside means the slanting word goes around the musical letter

parts.note: slopy is a dictionary word for sloping, at an angle
P is piano, the musical direction for playing softly

explanation.surface: Something leaning gently over turns out to be soaking.
explanation.walkthrough: SLOPY is a dictionary word meaning sloping; P (piano, softly in music) goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy ground or food is wet and slushy, full of liquid.

clue.text: Assistant first-class from around Paris

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI in crosswords
de is French for from, the word used around Paris

explanation.surface: A top-class helper has come from somewhere near Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is written with the letters A and I in crosswords; 'from around Paris' asks for the French word for 'from'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is a helper or assistant, often to an official.

clue.text: Ode old man composed forecasting disaster

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: An elderly man wrote a poem predicting catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom-laden means heavy with foreboding, predicting a grim outcome.

clue.text: Delay prisoner coming after what he received

indicators.note: coming after places the prisoner's word behind the sentence's word

parts.note: a prisoner receives a sentence, or time
a lag is a convict, as in old lag

explanation.surface: A convict arrives after hearing his sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: LAG is British slang for a convict ('old lag'); 'what he received' is the TIME he was sentenced to.
explanation.definitionFit: A time lag is an interval or delay between two related events.

clue.text: In line for a rise

parts.note: a crease is a line, as in a fold

explanation.surface: Someone is in the queue for a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: An increase is a growth or rise in amount.

clue.text: Thrilling going to include Charlie

indicators.note: to include means to take in, so the missing letter is placed within the going word

parts.note: exiting means going or leaving
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A trip becomes exciting once Charlie comes along.
explanation.definitionFit: Exciting means causing great enthusiasm, just as thrilling does.

clue.text: Stick with New Testament disciple

parts.note: to stick is to adhere

explanation.surface: A follower sticks with the Gospels.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or supporter of a leader or cause.

clue.text: New US city a loner's wandering round

indicators.note: wandering round suggests the letters drift about into a new order

parts.note: taken letter for letter, including the S

explanation.surface: A solitary traveller roams around an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic hint: 'New' plus this word gives the US city New Orleans.
explanation.definitionFit: Orleans preceded by New names the Louisiana city, so 'New' points to the word itself.

clue.text: Second peak that's the most dangerous

parts.note: Everest is the highest mountain peak

explanation.surface: A climber reflects that the second summit is the riskiest.
explanation.definitionFit: Severest means harshest or most serious, so most dangerous.

clue.text: Tape some made more of

indicators.note: some means a portion of, so part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone recorded a tape with more of their work.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is a demonstration recording, often a tape sent to record labels.

clue.text: Caution about entering colony

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the short word sits inside the caution word

parts.note: to caution is to warn
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A warning is issued about entering a settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A warren is a network of burrows housing a colony of rabbits.

clue.text: Penny turning blue at old American Indian village

indicators.note: turning means changing, so the colour word's letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A penny goes blue at an ancient native settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges the colour word to UEBL, which sits between the penny and 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pueblo is a Native American village of adobe houses in the US Southwest.

clue.text: One's main holiday perhaps

parts.note: the main is the sea, so a main holiday is a holiday at sea, not one's chief vacation

explanation.surface: A person describes their principal getaway of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: A voyage taken on a ship for pleasure is a holiday on the main, the sea.

clue.text: Turn pale with certain enjoyment

indicators.note: turn means change, so the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone goes white while sure of their delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' looks like 'become', as in 'turn pale', but it rearranges PALE to PLEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure is a feeling of enjoyment or happy satisfaction.

clue.text: Married woman's ill-will

parts.note: Alice is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A wife's resentment toward someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the intention to do harm, a hostile feeling.

clue.text: Fit lady in who is very attractive

indicators.note: in means the lady's name is placed inside the word for fit

parts.note: fit means able
Dora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A fit young woman is found to be charming.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable describes someone delightful and charming, very attractive.

clue.text: Tailless bird returned to ice floe

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the trimmed bird is read backwards
tailless means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: A bird missing its tail comes back to a floating sheet of ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' drops GREBE's last E to give GREB, and 'returned' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A berg, short for iceberg, is a large floating mass of ice.

clue.text: Go to bed, with painful disorder arising in the morning

parts.note: to turn in is to go to bed
gout is a painful inflammation of the joints

explanation.surface: Someone retires to bed while a painful complaint flares up by daybreak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go to bed' looks like the definition, but it is TURN IN; the definition is the opposite action, getting up.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning out is an idiom for getting out of bed in the morning.
